evidence: Liv. 40.29: siccitāte et inopiā frūgum īnsignis annus fuit
Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.1: praesertim maximā siccitāte
terms.comment: The ordinary word in prose, in the singular and, of seasons of drought, in the plural.

phrases.latin: Tantā siccitāte hortus āret; age, rigēmus.
phrases.english: The garden is parched with all this dry weather; come on, let’s water it.

phrases.latin: siccitāte et inopiā frūgum īnsignis annus fuit. sex mēnsēs numquam plūvisse memoriae prōditum.
phrases.english: The year was remarkable for drought and a shortage of crops; it is recorded that for six months it never rained.

phrases.latin: quod eō annō frūmentum in Galliā propter siccitātēs angustius prōvēnerat
phrases.english: because that year the corn crop in Gaul had been poorer on account of the droughts

phrases.latin: aquamque, quam iī dūcēbant nōn longē ā vīllā, bellē sānē fluentem vīdī, praesertim maximā siccitāte
phrases.english: and I saw the water they were bringing not far from the house flowing very nicely, especially in so great a drought
